comment: Identity registry vectors, run by ocaml/identity/test (Mesh_identity) and by tests/identity-registry.test.ts (respawn.py). Each case starts from a registry, applies its steps (a claim, with the incarnations the PTY host lists when known, or a prune with the incarnations to keep) and compares the result; resolve asks what a restore would read. Each file is a registry file's text and what reading it gives. A merge keeps one active holder of an id among the incarnations it compares. A launch over a lost offer may leave two active holders of one id (the lost offer's entry is set aside, then kept unchanged); no case runs two agents on it, since a launch and a restore are refused while a listed session holds the id.

cases.name: a first claim is inserted
the same id from a stronger source upgrades the entry; the generation stays
a weaker report of the same id changes nothing
a listing binds the created of a chosen entry and fills its start time; holds_open is never taken back
another id replaces the entry: a hook of the same process (a /clear), then a listing of a later process
a late report of a process that has quit is ignored
another agent counts only from a process started after the entry
I4: a stronger source takes the conversation, the holder is contested
I4: a weaker claim is contested and the holder keeps the conversation
I4: equal sources, the one that holds the rollout open wins
I4: equal sources and neither holds it: the current holder keeps it; a repeated claim changes nothing
the contest ends when the holder is gone and the session claims the conversation again
two agents may name the same id string: no contest
prune keeps the listed and the young entries, binds the listing's created, drops the rest
invalid claims change nothing
the agents' id formats
an observation never takes back a hook or chosen id of the same process; one of a later process does
the same id seen from a later process keeps that start time: a late report of an earlier one is ignored
the same id from another agent of a later process replaces the entry, its agent included
two partial records of one incarnation joined by a claim become one: the newest
two partial records of one incarnation joined by a prune become one: the newest
a holder the PTY host does not list loses to a claim of a listed incarnation, whatever the sources
I4 among listed incarnations: a weaker claim is contested, the holder keeps the conversation
neither incarnation listed: I4, the holder keeps the conversation
a holder keyed by its nonce only is listed when the listing gives that nonce: I4
an untimed report of another id keeps the known start of the same process
a refused claim still binds the incarnation it joins

files.name: a newer version is read as empty and is not replaced
an older version is read as empty
a truncated file is read as empty
bad entries and a repeated incarnation are dropped; a missing generation is the highest entry's
